selection_rationale: Select c1_gvr_semantic_eval: highest immediate feasibility and direct alignment with the programme focus (reliability/safety of LLM-generated NetOps configs). Critic review returned ‘pass’ and listed concrete, addressable design repairs (verifier specification, preregistration of prompts/seeds, human-inspection plan). The paired, controlled GVR vs schema vs unconstrained design is falsifiable, reproducible at scale within the manifest compute limits, and directly tests semantic invariants valued by the CNSM track.
unresolved_uncertainties: Deterministic verifier incompleteness: verifier may miss semantic invariants (false negatives).
Repair-loop overfitting: repairs may simply chase verifier checks without preserving operational desirability.
Prompt/seed sensitivity: single-model/prompt susceptibility and variability under different prompts or seeds.
Task-bank representativeness: synthetic/public tasks may not capture production topology/vendor diversity (external validity).
Human-inspection reliability: sampling rate, labeling protocol, and inter-rater agreement for qualitative checks remain to be specified.
required_repairs_before_preregistration: Specify exact deterministic verifier implementation(s), version(s), and formal invariant definitions (reachability, ACL semantics) with canonical oracle test cases to validate verifier soundness.
Preregister exact LLM model identifier(s), model-version hash, all prompts verbatim (generation, schema constraints, repair prompts), and random-seed policy for reproducibility.
Define repair-prompt templates, allowed bounded edit operations, deterministic stopping rules (max attempts=3, timeout policy), and how verifier timeouts are handled.
Publish dataset-generation procedure and release the public task bank (topologies, intents, policies) and generation scripts or stable subsets; include licensing/ provenance notes.

Increase and preregister human-inspection plan: sampling fraction, labeling instructions, inter-rater training, adjudication rules, and inclusion of golden-reference tasks to estimate human/verifier error rates.
Preregister analysis details exactly: primary comparisons (C vs A, C vs B), statistical tests (paired McNemar), multiple-comparison correction, covariates, and planned subgroup/failure-mode analyses.
